newsitem.title: USA: Issuers should get break on yield burning--lawyers.
newsitem.headline: Issuers should get break on yield burning--lawyers.

text.p: The IRS should not seek "yield burning" penalities against bond issuers that did not know their dealers were overcharging them for U.S. Treasuries, municipal bond lawyers said Tuesday.
The National Association of Bond Lawyers made the recommendation in a 19-page comment letter to the Internal Revenue Service.
IRS in July said issuers of advance refunding bonds can enter into "closing agreements" with the IRS to head off possibly having the interest on their bonds declared taxable.
Municipalities would have to pay Treasury the difference between the price they paid and the spot price of the securities on the purchase date, plus interest, the IRS said in Revenue Procedure 96-49.

"As a result of the revenue procedure, issuers who did not know or have reason to know of potential overpayments are being forced to spend time and money attempting to self-audit their transactions," NABL said. "All of this seems unnecessary and unfair."
NABL said IRS should excuse unknowing issuers, as long as they cooperate with any IRS or Securities and Exchange Commission investigations of pricing of open market securities, NABL said.
